theme: Spelling vs. real sound (Pause / Carry / Change)

threads.text:
Quick Korean ear test 👂

How do Koreans actually say 국물 (soup broth)?

A) 국물
B) 궁물
C) 국믈

Drop your answer before reading the replies 👇

You learned 입니다 letter by letter.

But no Korean says ip-ni-da.
They say [임니다] — the ㅂ melts into ㅁ before ㄴ.

That's why you can read Korean perfectly and still miss it in a K-drama.

Which word surprised you the first time you heard it spoken?

Most Korean learners don't have a vocabulary problem.
They have a listening gap: spelling ≠ sound.

So we built K-Listen around one loop:
hear it → notice what you heard → hear it again → then the why.

No rules to memorize first. Just your ear.

What's the hardest part of Korean listening for you?

instagram.caption:
You can read these 5 Korean words… but you probably hear them wrong 👂

Korean isn't pronounced letter by letter. When sounds meet, they pause, carry over, or change — and that's exactly why K-dramas feel too fast.

Which one surprised you most? Tell me in the comments 👇

slides.why: ㅂ meets ㄴ and melts into a nasal ㅁ.
ㅌ meets 이 and shifts forward to ㅊ.
ㅎ fades away before a vowel.
ㄱ meets ㅎ and comes out with a puff of breath.
ㄴ meets ㄹ — and the ㄹ wins.
